rows.rationale: A keeps each defect, consequence, location, ID, and fix together in one user-focused list. B preserves the facts but separates findings from actions, repeats metadata, and makes the reader cross-reference IDs.

B leads with the concrete defect and gives a direct, complete requested change. A is accurate but its ID, priority, and topic prefix add visual and cognitive overhead without improving the inline guidance.
B states the ref-resolution defect as the heading, preserves the reproducibility consequence, and makes the network/offline split an explicit request. A is complete but reads more like ledger output.
B separates the two required changes into a short action list, making the parser migration and offline test easier to recall. No fact or action is lost.
B preserves both failure modes and presents finite-value validation and invalid-row accounting as distinct actions. A is correct but denser and less directive.

A foregrounds the concrete field defect and cleanly separates the new-snapshot and legacy-snapshot actions. B contains the same substance but the ledger prefix and compressed prose make it less immediately actionable.
B is direct and concise: it names the live-mode miss and explicitly requests querying present-null entries while preserving offline behavior. A is equally factual but less natural and directive.
B presents the exact-ID precedence and uniqueness condition as two crisp imperatives. A preserves both actions but its metadata prefix and tentative phrasing add friction.

B co-locates each defect, mechanism, consequence, location, ID, and complete fix path. A is factually complete, but its table and separate plan section force ID-based cross-referencing and substantially increase cognitive load.

A explicitly retains all three actions: preflight every new record, preserve recoverable old files through writes and route transitions, and test mid-write rollback across routes. B clearly explains the defect but does not explicitly carry forward the preflight-all-records action, which is an action-recall loss.

A names the unstable identity input precisely and gives a direct instruction distinguishing the raw source path from reconciled metadata and routing. B is natural and accurate, but its ledger prefix and tentative action wording weaken action recall.

A directly requests atomic replacement and explicitly covers failures, exclusions, clean runs, and preservation of the last complete ledger. B preserves those facts but presents the fix tentatively and with extra ledger metadata.

B gives the two merge-readiness defects with locations, IDs, mechanisms, and actions in one compact section, then keeps all four low suggestions complete. A preserves the content but splits findings from plans and adds a table and operational ledger detail that make the report harder to scan.

A clearly explains why the warning is hidden, preserves PR #221 as the prerequisite, and directly requests the default-rich CLI check. B is accurate but the metadata prefix and softer wording reduce immediacy.

A precisely identifies the required guide path and directly asks for the three required content points. B preserves the facts and action but adds ledger metadata and uses tentative phrasing, making the requested change less forceful.
